title: The plan to finish A1 (A2 parked until A1 ships)
ask: docs/PLAN_A1_FINISH.md in the 51.04 folder. A1 is finished when every card has natural, stress-marked Lithuanian, your voice, an approved picture, and rc5 is built, checked on your phone and uploaded. Phase 1, yours: the 3 takes, the stress sheets (97 A1 forms), the 19 clipped July takes (batch 2 page), Round 7, the AnkiWeb description, and the duplicate-sentence policy. Phase 2, the next session's agents: apply your answers, draw Ką daryti?, fix the study-order generator (it no longer reproduces the frozen order; nothing changed, it was caught and reverted), add build checks, and a final picture QA sweep. Phase 3: rc5, verification, your phone check, upload. Duplicate sentences, my proposal: a phrase card and its cloze card may share a sentence on purpose; only true duplicates of the same kind get fixed (e.g. 0043/0103 Atsiprašau).

(your word-order fix is in), and 'Ką daryti?' once its picture exists. They are the first takes on recorder_A2.html. detail:
*Executor, 2026-10-19; counts updated 2026-10-20 after the key rename and the proofreading return. The sheet: `recorder_A2.html` at the repo root. Its list: `data/recording_list.csv`. Both come from `python3 build_recorder.py A2`.*

## What is on the sheet
The sheet lists every take that the current deck still needs: **2,849 takes**. The A1 subdeck comes first, then A2, each in study order (`study_order.csv`, study order v3; same order as `data/recording_order_v3.csv`).

| | takes | of which |
|---|---|---|
| **A1** (takes 1–988) | **988** | 952 new · 20 replace the synthetic voice · 16 re-takes |
| **A2** (takes 989–2,849) | **1,861** | 1,788 new · 73 replace the synthetic voice |
| kinds | | 1,813 words · 981 example sentences (`<key>_s`) · 55 sentence cards |

By kind: **A1** 619 word takes · 334 example sentences · 35 sentence cards (369 sentence takes in all);
**A2** 1,194 word takes · 647 example sentences · 20 sentence cards (667 sentence takes).
Every take is named by its card key (`NNNN_slug`, spec §12); the number on the take is the card's plate number.

These takes are not on the sheet:
- the 415 base-deck cards and 150 A2-list cards whose July takes still match the card;
- the 31 B1-deferred rows and the 4 merged-away keys.

**Re-takes (16, all A1; a red "re-take" badge shows the old words):**
- The words are now wrong, so the old take has been withdrawn and the card is silent until you re-record it:
  - 1124_lupos *lūpos* (was *lūpa*);
  - 1082_mobilusis_telefonas *mobilusis telefonas · mobiliojo telefono* (the old genitive was wrong);
  - 0836_rugsejis *rugsėjis · rugsėjo* (was *rugsėjio*);
  - 0923_cekis *čekis* (was *kvitas*);
  - 0521_prasom_pakartoti *Prašom pakartoti*;
  - 0565_prasom_uzrasyti *Prašom užrašyti*.
- The ten colours (0617_raudonas … 0626_pilkas) said the genitive (*raudonas · raudono*). The card now shows the feminine (*raudonas · raudona*). The old takes are correct Lithuanian and stay in the deck until you replace them.

The other wording changes were never recorded, so they appear as ordinary new takes in their new wording: 0203_prasom_kalbeti_leciau *Prašom kalbėti lėčiau*, 1029_prasom_sestis *Prašom sėstis*, 2136_ar_galite_ka_nors *…parekomenduoti?*, 1653_pakartoti_s, 1112_sestis_s.

The proofreading return of 2026-10-20 changed 26 sentences or headwords (`rounds/2026-10-20_proofread/returned_plan_v1.md`); none of them had been recorded, so they are ordinary new takes in the corrected wording (e.g. 0331_kelinta_valanda *Kelinta valanda?*, 1006_uzsiemimas *užsiėmimas*, 2360_apsidrausti *apsidrausti*, 2392_rakinti_s *Kai rakino duris, atėjo kaimynas.*).

**Takes recorded under the old card names** (the A2-list ids, the three-digit base keys and the sentence ids of before the rename, and the five keys re-slugged on 2026-10-20; all listed in `data/key_maps/key_map_v*.csv`) are not lost: when you click *Enable microphone & start*, the regenerated sheet moves each stored clip to its new key together with the words it was recorded for, and says how many it carried over. A clip whose words have since changed is set aside (in *Export all*, folder `superseded/`); nothing is deleted. Tested headless on 2026-10-20 (`rounds/2026-10-20_rename/recorder_migration_test_v2.txt`). Still: press **Export all** once in the old sheet before opening the new one, as a safety copy.

## How to record
1. **On the Mac**, open this file in **Chrome**: `~/Library/CloudStorage/ProtonDrive-…/50-59 Languages & Learning Method/51 Lithuanian Language & Culture/51.04 Lithuanian Flashcard Project/recorder_A2.html`. You can double-click it in Finder and choose *Open With → Google Chrome*. Use the same browser every time, because your takes are kept in that browser's storage. Safari and Firefox are untested for local files.
2. Click **Enable microphone & start**. The sheet jumps to the first take that has not been recorded yet.
3. Read everything in the dashed box: the headword, then its forms, one breath apart. The *italic* line under the word is the stressed form; say it that way. For sentences, read the sentence once, naturally.
4. Press **Space** to start. Wait for "SPEAK NOW" (0.4 s), speak, then press **Space** again. With auto-advance on, the sheet moves to the next take. **P** plays the take back; **←/→** move between takes.

**Phone:** opening the file on a phone does not work, because the microphone and the stored takes need a web address. Record on the Mac.

**Session size:** about **100 takes**, roughly 30 minutes at ~15 s a take. The A1 share is about 4 hours in all, so about 10 sessions. Stop when your voice tires; the sheet resumes where you left off.

## After each session: Export new
- Click **⬇ Export new takes**. You get one ZIP with only the takes recorded since the last export (`lt_A2_takes_<date>_batch.zip`). Batches add up; a re-recorded take goes out again in the next batch.
- **Put the ZIP in** `media/audio/_inbox/` in the project folder (since the deep tidy of 2026-10-24; a ZIP dropped in the old `a2_build/audio/inbox/` is still found). ZIPs there are not committed to git. Then tell the executor: "audio batch in the inbox".
- **Export all** is the safety copy. It holds every take in the browser, plus older clips the sheet has set aside (`superseded/`, `off_list/`). Use it once at the end, or before clearing the browser.

## What happens next (executor)
1. The executor (`python3 tools/ingest_takes.py --inbox`) converts each clip to the `dest` path in `data/recording_list.csv` (`media/audio/<key>.mp3` for every card since the tidy of 2026-10-24; before that `audio/` for the 520-word base and `audio_a2/` for the rest) and writes the key's row in `audio_source.tsv`, including what was said. A take it replaces moves to `media/audio/_history/`.
2. When the sheet is regenerated, recorded takes drop off it. The browser storage name stays fixed (`lt_recorder_A2_afb2ebe2`), so regenerating never loses a take.
3. If a card's words change later, its stored take is set aside, not deleted, and the card comes back as a re-take.

title: Listen: batch 1 (54 takes), original vs processed
ask: All 54 are processed and in the deck: start clicks removed with 250 ms of silence kept before your voice, end clicks removed where safely possible, nothing cut within 250 ms of your speech, the original of every take kept. No re-recordings needed. Listen at least to the 10 marked takes at the top of the page (8 keep a short sound just after the words: a final consonant or the stop click, taip most likely to matter; 2 had the closing click lowered instead of cut). Two decisions in the note: (1) loudness: your new takes come out about 2 dB quieter than July, because July was evidently peak-limited and this processing uses plain gain only; matching July needs a gentle limiter (2–5 dB on peaks). title: AnkiWeb description and the choices in it
ask: The text is below, with the final counts (1,191 cards). Decide: (1) sign it with your name, or keep "the author"; (2) the share title; (3) the tags; (4) replace the old v2.0 share, or keep both; (5) licence CC BY-NC 4.0, as in the repo's LICENSE. Write your choices in the note.
options: Approve with the changes in my note
detail:
### The text

**Lietuvių Flashcards — A1 (v3.0)**

Lithuanian from zero to A1 through pictures, phrases and sentences. The first of two subdecks; A2 follows as a separate package.

**What is in the deck**

1,191 cards, ordered by usefulness: survival words and everyday phrases come first.

- 687 picture cards for words
- 135 phrase cards (greetings, thanks, asking for things)
- 334 cloze cards for function words and forms
- 35 sentence cards with a picture

**How a card works**

The front shows a picture with an English caption in the band below it. The back gives the Lithuanian word with its stress mark, gender and forms (genitive, present and past, or the feminine), and the English gloss. Phrase cards add a note on when to use the phrase. Cloze cards show a Lithuanian sentence with a blank and the English as a hint; sentence cards pair the blank with a picture.

Stress marks are taken from Wiktionary, kirtis.info and the LKŽ, never guessed.

**The pictures**

The art is an original house style: a civil-defence training manual from a free Lithuania of 1981. The pictures are AI-generated in that style and reviewed by hand. A few cards show real interwar places and people: the Lituanica with Darius and Girėnas, Basanavičius as the doctor, Čiurlionis as the artist, with a painting after one of his public-domain works on the easel.

**Audio**

547 cards carry recordings by the author, a native speaker, reading the word and its forms. 20 older cards still use a synthetic voice, and the other 624 are silent until the next update.

Fonts: Brygada 1918 (SIL Open Font Licence), embedded. In night mode, leave image inversion off.

**Upgrading from an earlier version**

The note types changed in v3.0. Delete the old deck before importing this one; study history from older versions does not carry over. The card IDs will be locked once the A2 subdeck is out; from then on, updates import in place and keep your progress. Until then, an update may ask you to delete and re-import.

**Licence and credits**

CC BY-NC 4.0: share and adapt for non-commercial use, with credit and a link to the source. Word list from the Fluent Forever 625, extended from A1 English word lists. Pictures, data and recordings by the author.

Source and issues: https://github.com/dainius-sileika/Lithuanian_Flashcards

### The choices, with background

1. **Licence wording.** The repo `LICENSE` is CC BY-NC 4.0 (not BY-NC-SA) and names the owner in the required attribution string. The text follows it. If a different licence is wanted for the published deck, change `LICENSE` first, then this line.
2. **Signing the description.** The rule "name no living person" was applied to the owner too: the text says "the author" and leaves the credit to the GitHub link and `LICENSE`. Decide whether to sign it with a name.
3. **Audio sentence.** The brief said "the 520 core cards have native-speaker recordings"; the data says otherwise. `audio_source.tsv` marks 427 recordings as human and 93 as `azure-neural` (the files differ: 48 kbps, no ID3 tag). On 2026-10-19, of the 446 base cards in the A1 block, 427 were human, 18 synthetic, 1 without audio (`0007_batonas`); the 75 base rows with `level = A2` are exactly the 75 remaining synthetic ones. If the 18 were re-recorded without updating the ledger, correct the ledger first. The retag for order v3 may move some of these between subdecks; recount from the manifest.
4. **Historical cards left out on purpose.** Gustaitis (2263_inzinierius), the 1939 basketball team (138 komanda, `level = A2`; 1405_krepsinis) and the two posters (*Velnio nuotaka* on 1473_siaip_sau, *Milžino paunksmė* on 1419_spektaklis) are A2-level rows and not in this package. They belong in the A2 description. 097 prezidentas and 123 autorius ship without likenesses. If order v3 retags any of them A1, add them to "The pictures".
5. **Title** for the AnkiWeb share, e.g. "Lietuvių Flashcards — Lithuanian A1 (pictures, audio, stress marks)". Decide also whether the v2.0 share is replaced or kept (F3).
6. **Tags** on AnkiWeb, e.g. `lithuanian lietuvių a1 vocabulary pictures audio`.

title: Proofreading: your 25 corrections, how they went in
ask: 11 went in as you wrote them. 2 cards switch to your word, because it wasn't a card yet: veikla → užsiėmimas (Mėgstu užsiėmimus lauke.) and draustis → apsidrausti (Prieš kelionę reikia apsidrausti.). For 13, your sentence dropped the word the card teaches. Mostly your word already has its own card (Kiek jums metų?, Peršalau, šiek tiek, du kartus, reikia, užrakinti…); in the rest the old word is worth keeping as a card. So these cards keep their word in a new everyday sentence. Your sentence is saved as the reason. Kuri valanda? becomes Kelinta valanda?, and the kelinta card gets Kelinta šiandien? instead. Below are the 13 new sentences: if one sounds off, write your version in the note, otherwise nothing to do. One side effect: the usage note on the back of Kelinta valanda? was withdrawn, because it explained Kuri valanda?.
